original_value: As an e-commerce feature, the personalized recommendation is invariably highly-valued by both consumers and merchants. The e-tourism has become one of the hottest industries with the adoption of recommendation systems. Several lines of evidence have confirmed the travel-product recommendation is quite different from traditional recommendations. Travel products are usually browsed and purchased relatively infrequently compared with other traditional products (e.g., books and food), which gives rise to the extreme sparsity of travel data. Meanwhile, the choice of a suitable travel product is affected by an army of factors such as departure, destination, and financial and time budgets. To address these challenging problems, in this article, we propose a Probabilistic Matrix Factorization with Multi-Auxiliary Information (PMF-MAI) model in the context of the travel-product recommendation. In particular, PMF-MAI is able to fuse the probabilistic matrix factorization on the user-item interaction matrix with the linear regression on a suite of features constructed by the multiple auxiliary information. In order to fit the sparse data, PMF-MAI is built by a whole-data based learning approach that utilizes unobserved data to increase the coupling between probabilistic matrix factorization and linear regression. Extensive experiments are conducted on a real-world dataset provided by a large tourism e-commerce company. PMF-MAI shows an overwhelming superiority over all competitive baselines on the recommendation performance. Also, the importance of features is examined to reveal the crucial auxiliary information having a great impact on the adoption of travel products.

result.paraphrase: In e-commerce, personalized recommendations are highly valued by both consumers and merchants. With the rise of recommendation systems, e-tourism has become one of the hottest industries. Evidence shows that travel-product recommendation differs markedly from traditional recommendation tasks. Compared with products such as books and food, travel items are bought and browsed far less often, creating extreme sparsity in travel data. In addition, selecting an appropriate travel product depends on many factors, including departure point, destination, and budget constraints in both money and time. To tackle these challenges, this article proposes a Probabilistic Matrix Factorization with Multi-Auxiliary Information (PMF-MAI) model for travel-product recommendation. PMF-MAI combines probabilistic matrix factorization on the user-item interaction matrix with linear regression over features derived from multiple auxiliary information sources. To handle sparse data, it uses a whole-data-based learning strategy that incorporates unobserved data to strengthen the coupling between probabilistic matrix factorization and linear regression. Extensive experiments on a real-world dataset from a major tourism e-commerce company show that PMF-MAI outperforms all competing baselines by a wide margin. The study also analyzes feature importance to identify the key auxiliary information that strongly influences travel-product adoption.
